## What doing it consciously looks like

Some of this came from thinking. Most came from getting it wrong. I’m still testing parts of it.

Before making love, talk about jealousy, attraction to other people, stress, old patterns, how recent the healing is, what you want from each other when things go bad, and money. Don’t only ask what somebody believes. Give them a situation: “If X happened, what would you want? What would you probably do?” If the answer is still abstract, there usually isn’t much of an answer yet.

Then stop. Go be normal together. Ten profound talks in one weekend can feel deep because you had ten profound talks, not because you know each other. Some things you have to watch.

Don’t let one yes answer everything else either. Sex does not answer whether to move in. Moving in does not answer whether this is the person to build a life with. Housing can make separate living difficult, but sharing a home starts narrowing choices for practical reasons. Set a real date to ask how it’s going before there’s a crisis. A wonderful lover can still be a terrible co-parent, community member, or life partner. And “I’m taking a chance on this person” is not the same thing as “this is the right person.”

Make deep friends together. Your old friends will be partial. Fine. You still want some people who know both of you.

Keep your own practices too. If being loved makes you stop learning to love and regulate yourself, something went wrong. And if some part of you says, Wait. Slow down. Something doesn’t fit. I need to ask this, ask it before chemistry talks you out of it.
